【参考范文 · 164 词】写作无唯一标准答案，以下为达标示范
Nowadays, more and more students have realized the importance of self-discipline in their personal growth. In an age flooded with short videos and endless distractions, the ability to control oneself has become the very foundation of academic success and character building.
A vivid example is my roommate Li Ming. When we entered university, he set himself a firm rule: no phone before finishing the day's study plan. While others drifted from one game to another, his steady self-management allowed him to master a difficult programming course and win a national scholarship. His experience convinced me that talent alone rarely decides how far a person goes; it is perseverance and daily self-control that truly shape our future.
Therefore, I firmly believe that cultivating self-discipline deserves our full attention. Rather than blaming the environment for our failures, we should learn to say no to temptations and stick to our own plans. Only by mastering ourselves can we grow into the people we truly wish to become.

lines.en: W: Hi, Alan. Sorry for not calling you back sooner. You said on the phone you had something you needed to discuss with me?
lines.zh: W: 嗨，艾伦。抱歉没能早点给你回电话。你在电话里说有件事想和我讨论？

lines.en: M: Well, to get right down to it, I'm having second thoughts about my major. With my family situation getting more complicated and the end of my university education nearing, persisting with Art History just doesn't seem the right choice.
lines.zh: M: 好吧，直说了吧，我开始重新考虑自己的专业了。随着家里的情况变得越来越复杂，而我也即将结束大学学业，坚持学艺术史似乎已经不是正确的选择了。

lines.en: W: Alan, in the last 3 years, I have heard nothing but how passionate you are about the Art History programme. You often told fellow classmates how fabulous the instructors were and that you finally felt accepted. What would cause you to abandon it?
lines.zh: W: 艾伦，过去三年里，我听到的全都是你对艺术史专业有多么热情。你经常告诉同学们这里的老师有多么出色，还说自己终于有了归属感。究竟是什么让你想放弃它？

lines.en: M: My father's current financial situation has helped me realize that a more financially viable employment opportunity is not necessarily a bad thing. Art History nourishes my soul, but does nothing to put food on my plate.
lines.zh: M: 我父亲目前的经济状况让我意识到，选择一个经济上更可行的就业机会未必是件坏事。艺术史滋养了我的心灵，却无法解决我的温饱问题。

lines.en: W: What about all the work opportunities I discussed with you last month? Have you gone to those places of business to investigate whether any legitimate positions might be available for someone with your background?
lines.zh: W: 那我上个月和你谈过的那些工作机会呢？你有没有去那些公司了解一下，看看是否有适合你这种背景的人担任的正规职位？

lines.en: M: Ah, well…
lines.zh: M: 啊，这个嘛……

lines.en: W: Look, Alan, if your heart is set on working in the art industry, you need to be more assertive and start talking with people. Networking is key if you want to become a celebrity in the world of museums and galleries.
lines.zh: W: 听我说，艾伦，如果你一心想在艺术行业工作，就得更加主动，开始和人交流。如果你想成为博物馆和画廊界的名人，人脉是关键。

lines.en: M: Time is a very precious commodity right now. My social life does not exist. I can barely keep up with my studies and thesis is due by the end of this year. When can I find time to research jobs when I have so much to do as it is?
lines.zh: M: 现在时间非常宝贵。我的社交生活根本不存在。我连学业都勉强应付得来，而论文要在今年年底前提交。我已经有这么多事情要做，哪儿还有时间去研究工作呢？

lines.en: W: What you do now will determine your future options. Now is the optimum time to put forth your best effort.
lines.zh: W: 你现在所做的一切将决定你未来的选择。现在正是拿出最大努力的最佳时机。

lines.en: M: I will take what you said into consideration. The advice is much appreciated.
lines.zh: M: 我会考虑你说的话。非常感谢你的建议。

lines.en: M: Have you decided yet what your end-of-semester business project will be on?
lines.zh: M：你决定好学期末的商业项目要做什么了吗？

lines.en: W: Yes. How about you?
lines.zh: W：决定了。你呢？

lines.en: M: Yes. Go on. You go first.
lines.zh: M：我也决定了。你先说吧。

lines.en: W: I am going to do it about beef.
lines.zh: W：我打算做牛肉方面的项目。

lines.en: M: Beef?
lines.zh: M：牛肉？

lines.en: W: Yeah, beef. I'm going to design a business case study for a cow farm that supplies beef for the domestic market.
lines.zh: W：对，牛肉。我打算为一家向国内市场供应牛肉的养牛场设计一份商业案例研究。

lines.en: M: Well, that sounds very interesting and original. Wherever did you get that idea?
lines.zh: M：听起来确实很有意思，也很有新意。你到底是怎么想到这个点子的？

lines.en: W: I don't know. It just came to me, I guess. But think about it. Beef consumption has been rising strongly over the past 20 years. As the economy continues to grow, consumer demand is expected to continue to increase for the foreseeable future. And currently, most of the beef is imported, which brings with it added fees. So why not raise cattle here?
lines.zh: W：我也不知道。我想大概就是突然想到的吧。不过你想想，过去20年来，牛肉消费量一直在大幅增长。随着经济持续发展，预计在可预见的未来，消费者的需求还会继续增加。而且目前大部分牛肉都是进口的，这还会带来额外的费用。所以，我们为什么不在这里养牛呢？

lines.en: M: Of course. Makes perfect sense. There's plenty of land out west. So, if done right, it should be very profitable to raise our own cattle.
lines.zh: M：当然可以。完全说得通。西部有的是土地。所以，只要经营得当，自己养牛应该会非常赚钱。

lines.en: W: Exactly.
lines.zh: W：没错。

lines.en: M: Seriously, that sounds like a great idea. You should genuinely look into it once we get our degrees.
lines.zh: M：说真的，这听起来是个很棒的主意。等我们拿到学位后，你确实应该好好研究一下。

lines.en: W: Thanks. So, your turn now. What are you doing your case study on?
lines.zh: W：谢谢。现在轮到你了。你的案例研究要做什么？

lines.en: M: I was thinking about a car wash, but it now seems like such a boring notion after hearing your brilliant idea.
lines.zh: M：我原本在考虑洗车店，但听了你这个绝妙的主意后，我的想法现在显得太无聊了。

lines.en: W: That's cool. I could see that working. After all, there's plenty of cars about and those aren't going away any time soon. While many people don't care how their car looks, many other people do. You got yourself a vast and continual market.
lines.zh: W：这想法不错。我觉得能行。毕竟，车很多，而且短期内也不会减少。虽然很多人不在乎自己的车看起来怎么样，但也有很多人在乎。这样一来，你就拥有了一个庞大而持续的市场。

lines.en: M: Right. So the idea is a large self-cleaning car wash, but I mean really big and well-outfitted like they have in America. I was thinking of having it cater to high-end consumers in large cities. It could charge a profitable markup by offering just a bit more technical equipment and professional service than competitors.
lines.zh: M：对。所以我的想法是开一家大型自助洗车店，不过要像美国那种真正规模很大、设备齐全的洗车店。我考虑让它面向大城市里的高端消费者。只要比竞争对手多提供一些技术设备和专业服务，就可以收取有利可图的溢价。

lines.en: Increased television time for young children has long been linked with poorer progress in some areas of development. One possible way to counter those negative effects is talking while watching the screen. As a new study suggests, the more parents engaged in conversation with preschoolers during TV time, the more likely those children were to have higher curiosity levels when they reached kindergarten. This was particularly true for children with socioeconomic disadvantages.
lines.zh: 长期以来，幼儿看电视时间增加一直与其在某些发展领域进步较差有关。抵消这些负面影响的一种可能方式是在观看屏幕时进行交谈。一项新研究表明，父母在电视时间与学龄前儿童进行的对话越多，这些儿童进入幼儿园时表现出较高好奇心水平的可能性就越大。对于处于社会经济劣势的儿童而言，这一点尤其明显。

lines.en: "Our findings reinforce the importance of parent conversation to promote early childhood development and curiosity," said lead author Prachi Shah at University of Michigan Health C.S. Mott Children's Hospital. Researchers assessed hours of daily television exposure and frequency of parent-screen-time conversation among 1,500 preschoolers, and then measured early childhood curiosity in kindergarten. The study specifically focused on curiosity levels, which are associated with enhanced learning and higher academic achievement in reading and math at kindergarten, and behavioral-developmental benefits, especially for children from families with lower socioeconomic status. While many young children are now growing up with digital media exposure through mobile devices like tablets and phones, television remains a dominant screen activity, accounting for 72% of all screen time. TVs are in 98% of all homes, keeping television exposure a relevant developmental context in young children.
lines.zh: 密歇根大学健康中心C.S.莫特儿童医院的首席作者普拉奇·沙阿说：“我们的研究结果进一步证明，父母的对话对于促进幼儿早期发展和好奇心十分重要。”研究人员评估了1500名学龄前儿童每天接触电视的时长，以及父母在屏幕使用期间与孩子交谈的频率，随后测量了这些儿童进入幼儿园时的早期好奇心。该研究特别关注好奇心水平，因为好奇心与幼儿园阶段更强的学习能力、更高的阅读和数学学业成就，以及行为和发展方面的益处相关，尤其是对来自社会经济地位较低家庭的儿童而言。如今，许多幼儿通过平板电脑和手机等移动设备接触数字媒体，但电视仍然是主要的屏幕活动，占全部屏幕使用时间的72%。所有家庭中有98%拥有电视，这使电视接触仍然是幼儿发展中一个重要的环境因素。

lines.en: Excessive media exposure, including television, can displace exploratory activities such as play and parent-child interactions, which are believed to be key to cultivating curiosity in kids. "Our findings suggest the importance of parents finding opportunities to foster conversational exchanges in daily routines with their young children—including while watching television," Shah said.
lines.zh: 过度接触媒体，包括看电视，可能会挤占游戏和亲子互动等探索性活动，而这些活动被认为是培养儿童好奇心的关键。沙阿说：“我们的研究结果表明，父母应当在日常生活中寻找机会与幼儿进行对话交流，包括在观看电视时进行交流。”

lines.en: Humans are aspirational goal-seeking beings. Each of us, according to research, has an inborn drive to acquire. The "dark side" of this drive to acquire is being mindlessly driven to possess more and more "things" and to socially compare our "stuff" with all the stuff other people have in their lives. So the question is, how do we ensure we tap into our drive to acquire in positive ways that will benefit our well-being?
lines.zh: 人类是有抱负、追求目标的存在。研究表明，我们每个人天生都具有获取的驱动力。这种获取驱动力的“阴暗面”，在于不假思索地驱使自己拥有越来越多的“东西”，并将自己的“财物”与他人生活中拥有的一切进行社会比较。因此，问题在于，我们该如何确保以积极的方式运用这种获取驱动力，从而增进自身的幸福感？

lines.en: One way is to become more intentionally aspirational. To be intentionally aspirational includes consciously aspiring to be the person you need to be to succeed in your professional and personal life. It also includes consciously aspiring to acquire things in your life that will positively impact your sense of well-being. If you're not consciously, mindfully and intentionally harnessing this inborn drive to acquire, you might be mindlessly pursuing all the wrong things.
lines.zh: 一种方法是更加有意识地树立抱负。有意识地树立抱负，包括自觉追求成为一个能够在职业生活和个人生活中取得成功所需要成为的人。这也包括自觉追求获得生活中那些能够积极影响你幸福感的事物。如果你没有有意识、专注而明确地驾驭这种与生俱来的获取驱动力，就可能会在不假思索地追求所有错误的事物。

lines.en: While your intentional aspirational goals will include pursuit of acquiring things that will increase your sense of well-being, they ought to also include goals to help other people in your various life roles. Your intentional aspirational goals will also include striving to be your personal best—a person of "good" character, integrity, and trustworthiness.
lines.zh: 虽然你有意识树立的抱负目标会包括追求获得能够提升幸福感的事物，但这些目标也应包括在你所承担的各种生活角色中帮助他人的目标。你有意识树立的抱负目标还应包括努力做到最好的自己，成为一个具有“良好”品格、正直而值得信赖的人。

lines.en: Think about this from a practical, rather than theoretical viewpoint. If you're not pursuing intentional aspirational goals, you have nothing to strive for. If you have nothing to strive for, you're putting yourself in the dangerous position of simply drifting through life, and you will not be able to experience, live and enjoy all that life has to offer.
lines.zh: 请从实际而非理论的角度思考这一点。如果你没有追求有意识树立的抱负目标，就没有任何目标可供努力。如果你没有任何目标可供努力，就会使自己处于一种危险境地，只是在生活中随波逐流，也就无法体验、生活并享受人生所能提供的一切。

lines.en: It's revision time for exams and dissertations. The pressure is on, so you want all the help you can get to aid your memory and raise your grades. As a nutrition expert, I want to say that eating well can make a real difference to your revision regime—so what brain-boosting food and drink would I recommend?
lines.zh: 现在是准备考试和论文的复习阶段。压力很大，因此你希望得到一切可能的帮助来增强记忆力、提高成绩。作为一名营养专家，我想说，吃得健康能让你的复习安排产生显著不同，那么我会推荐哪些能增强大脑功能的食物和饮品呢？

lines.en: Coffee can have numerous benefits. However, while coffee may make you more alert, individuals can build up a tolerance, meaning this is short-lived. Coffee can also increase blood sugar and eventually cause lack of focus and energy. It's also worth noting that people react differently to coffee. Some people can drink it at midnight and go straight to sleep, whereas others get feelings of anxiety after a small amount. Also remember that coffee from a coffee shop may be stronger than coffee made at home. So stop drinking coffee by 2 pm and have a maximum of 2 cups of coffee a day, but be aware of your own reaction to it.
lines.zh: 咖啡有许多益处。然而，虽然咖啡可能会让你更加警觉，但人们会逐渐产生耐受性，这意味着这种效果是短暂的。咖啡还会升高血糖，最终导致注意力和精力不足。同样值得注意的是，人们对咖啡的反应各不相同。有些人可以在午夜喝咖啡后直接入睡，而另一些人只喝少量咖啡就会感到焦虑。还要记住，咖啡店的咖啡可能比家里冲的咖啡浓。因此，下午两点后就不要再喝咖啡了，每天最多喝两杯，但要留意自己对咖啡的反应。

lines.en: Whole grain foods will ward off hunger. Examples include porridge and whole wheat bread. Combining whole grain foods with protein will help keep your blood sugar levels balanced, which is essential for mood and concentration. Berries and nuts are a convenient and nutritious snack. Blueberries, like many dark colored fruits and vegetables, can slow down brain damage and age-related decline. Frozen berries are also a good choice. They are usually cheap, last longer and don't lose their nutrients when frozen. But flavored and coated nuts are less healthy as they contain added oil, salt, and sugar.
lines.zh: 全谷物食品可以防止饥饿。例子包括粥和全麦面包。将全谷物食品与蛋白质搭配食用，有助于保持血糖水平平衡，而这对情绪和注意力至关重要。浆果和坚果是方便又有营养的零食。蓝莓和许多深色水果、蔬菜一样，可以减缓大脑损伤和与年龄相关的衰退。冷冻浆果也是不错的选择。它们通常价格便宜、保存时间更长，而且冷冻后不会损失营养成分。但调味坚果和裹层坚果不那么健康，因为其中含有额外添加的油、盐和糖。

lines.en: Doctors often recommend taking vitamin supplements to top up on the nutrients you need. But I would say food should always come before supplements and the key to getting as many nutrients as possible is to eat a varied diet with lots of different colors such as frozen berries and dark green vegetables. It's better to get everything you need from food and drink. For example, oranges contain not only vitamin C which boosts the immune system, but also fiber and other components that you can't get packaged together in a tablet.
lines.zh: 医生经常建议服用维生素补充剂，以补充你所需的营养物质。但我认为，食物始终应该优先于补充剂，而获得尽可能多营养的关键，是食用包含多种不同颜色食物的多样化饮食，例如冷冻浆果和深绿色蔬菜。最好从食物和饮品中获取你所需要的一切。例如，橙子不仅含有能增强免疫系统的维生素C，还含有纤维和其他无法在一片药片中同时获得的成分。

lines.en: Don't forget to drink a proper amount of water, which can boost attention by almost 25 percent and can elevate your mood as well.
lines.zh: 别忘了饮用适量的水，这可以将注意力提高近25%，也能改善你的情绪。

lines.en: Finally, don't skip meals. Eating regularly will help keep blood sugar balanced and feed the brain with the fuel it needs.
lines.zh: 最后，不要不吃饭。规律进食有助于保持血糖平衡，并为大脑提供所需的能量。

lines.en: The late Swedish academic Hans Rosling has identified a worrying trend: not only do many people across advanced economies have no idea that the world is becoming a much better place, but they actually even think the opposite. This is no wonder, when the news focuses on reporting catastrophes, terrorist attacks, wars, and famines.
lines.zh: 已故瑞典学者汉斯·罗斯林发现了一个令人担忧的趋势：不仅许多发达经济体中的人们根本不知道世界正在变得越来越美好，实际上他们甚至认为情况恰恰相反。当新闻集中报道灾难、恐怖袭击、战争和饥荒时，这也就不足为奇了。

lines.en: Who wants to hear about the fact that every day some 200,000 people around the world are lifted above the $2-a-day poverty line? Or that more than 300,000 people get access to electricity and clean water for the first time every day? These stories in people in low-income countries simply don't make for exciting news coverage. But, as Rosling pointed out in his book Factfulness, it's important to put all the bad news in perspective.
lines.zh: 谁愿意听到这样的事实：世界各地每天约有20万人脱离每日2美元的贫困线？或者每天有超过30万人首次用上电并获得清洁饮用水？这些关于低收入国家民众的故事，确实难以成为令人兴奋的新闻报道内容。但是，正如罗斯林在他的《事实》一书中指出的那样，重要的是要把所有坏消息放在整体背景下加以看待。

lines.en: While it is true that globalization has put some downward pressure on middle-class wages in advanced economies in recent decades, it has also helped lift hundreds of millions of people above the global poverty line. If we really care about global welfare, globalization is the only way forward to ensure that economic prosperity is shared among all countries and not only a select few advanced economies.
lines.zh: 诚然，近几十年来，全球化对发达经济体中产阶级的工资造成了一定的下行压力，但它也帮助数亿人脱离了全球贫困线。如果我们确实关心全球福祉，那么全球化就是确保经济繁荣惠及所有国家，而不仅仅是少数发达经济体的唯一前进道路。

lines.en: While some people glorify the past, one of the big facts of economic history is that until quite recently a significant part of the world population has lived under quite miserable conditions—and this has been true throughout most of human history.
lines.zh: 虽然有些人美化过去，但经济史的一大事实是，直到相当晚近的时候，世界人口中仍有相当一部分生活在十分悲惨的条件下，而这在绝大部分人类历史时期一直如此。

lines.en: While there were many long-lasting ups and downs, like the Great Depression or the recent Great Recession, the constancy of the long-run growth rate is actually quite miraculous. Low-income countries, including China and India, have been growing at a significantly faster pace in recent decades and are quickly catching up to the West. A 10% growth rate over a prolonged period means that income levels double roughly every seven years. It is obviously good news if prosperity is more shared across the globe.
lines.zh: 尽管长期以来经历了许多持续时间较长的起伏，例如大萧条或近期的大衰退，但长期增长率的稳定性实际上相当不可思议。包括中国和印度在内的低收入国家，近几十年来一直以明显更快的速度增长，并且正在迅速追赶西方。长期保持10%的增长率，意味着收入水平大约每七年翻一番。如果繁荣能够在全球范围内得到更广泛的共享，这显然是个好消息。

lines.en: While inequality within countries has gone up as a result of globalization, global inequality has been on a steady downward trend for several decades. This is mostly a result of the improvement of hundreds of millions of people's living standards. In fact, for the first time ever since the Industrial Revolution, about half of the global population can be considered middle class.
lines.zh: 虽然全球化导致各国内部的不平等程度上升，但几十年来，全球不平等一直呈稳步下降趋势。这主要是数亿人的生活水平得到改善的结果。事实上，这是自工业革命以来，全球人口中约有一半首次可以被视为中产阶级。

lines.en: We all know that the sense of smell is powerful. The delicious scent of bread, for example, can act like a time machine. One sniff can bring back a memory from many years ago. Indeed, scent particles, in general, can revive memories that have been long forgotten. But why do smells sometimes trigger powerful memories, especially emotional ones? The short answer is that the brain regions that handle smells, memories and emotions are linked.
lines.zh: 我们都知道，嗅觉的力量十分强大。例如，面包的诱人香气就像一台时光机。闻一下，就能唤回许多年前的一段记忆。事实上，气味分子通常能够唤醒那些早已被遗忘的记忆。但为什么气味有时会触发强烈的记忆，尤其是情感记忆呢？简而言之，负责处理气味、记忆和情感的大脑区域彼此相连。

lines.en: A scent is a chemical particle that floats in through the nose and into the region of the brain responsible for smell, where the sensation is first processed into a form that the brain can read. Brain cells then carry that information to the area of the brain where emotions are processed, and then to an adjacent area of the brain where learning and memory formation take place.
lines.zh: 气味是一种化学微粒，它经由鼻腔飘入大脑中负责嗅觉的区域，在那里，这种感觉首先被处理成大脑能够读取的形式。随后，脑细胞将这些信息传递到负责处理情感的大脑区域，再传递到相邻的、负责学习和记忆形成的大脑区域。

lines.en: Scents are the only sensations that travel such a direct path to the emotional and memory centers of the brain. That results in an intimate connection between emotions, memories and scents, which is why memories triggered by scents are experienced as more emotional than those triggered by sight or sound.
lines.zh: 气味是唯一能够沿着如此直接的路径到达大脑情感中枢和记忆中枢的感觉。这就形成了情感、记忆和气味之间的密切联系，也正因如此，气味触发的记忆往往比视觉或听觉触发的记忆更具情感色彩。

lines.en: Let's take a closer look at how those memories are activated. Usually, when a person smells something that's connected to a meaningful event in their past, they'll first have an emotional response to the sensation and then a memory might follow. But sometimes, the memory doesn't come to the surface. The person might feel the emotion of something that happened in the past but won't remember what they experienced. What causes this baffling phenomenon? The explanation is context. Imagine this scenario—a person is walking down the street smelling a scent that they first encountered decades ago, which activates an emotional response. If the person had first come across that smell in a very different context, it will be much more difficult to recover the associated memory, because the brain uses the context to give meaning to the information and find that memory.
lines.zh: 让我们更仔细地看看这些记忆是如何被激活的。通常，当一个人闻到某种与过去某个重要事件有关的气味时，他首先会对这种感觉产生情绪反应，随后记忆可能会浮现出来。但有时，记忆并不会浮现。这个人可能会感受到过去发生的某件事所带来的情绪，却想不起自己当时经历了什么。是什么导致了这种令人困惑的现象？答案在于情境。想象这样一个场景：一个人走在街上，闻到一种他几十年前第一次接触到的气味，这激活了他的情绪反应。如果这个人当初是在一个截然不同的情境中第一次闻到这种气味的，那么他就会更难回忆起与之相关的记忆，因为大脑会利用情境赋予信息意义，并找出那段记忆。

lines.en: The special nature of memories brought back by scents notwithstanding, they have the same drawbacks as other memories. They aren't always accurate, and they can change over time. In fact, each time we remember something, that memory can become distorted. But, because of the strong emotional associations these memories evoke, people who remember something due to a scent are often convinced that the memories are accurate, even when they aren't.
lines.zh: 尽管气味唤回的记忆具有特殊性，但它们也存在与其他记忆相同的缺陷。它们并不总是准确的，而且会随着时间发生变化。事实上，每当我们回忆某件事时，那段记忆都有可能被扭曲。但是，由于这些记忆唤起了强烈的情感联系，那些因某种气味而回忆起某件事的人往往坚信自己的记忆是准确的，即使事实并非如此。

cloze.title: 2024年12月·第2套 英语六级完形填空（选词填空） · 26–35 题答案与解析

passages.en: Ever been talking about something important with someone you care about and found the discussion frustrating instead of fruitful? Negative energy can then cast a __(26)__ over your efforts to build a shared understanding.
passages.zh: 你是否曾经和在乎的人谈论某件重要的事情，却发现这场讨论令人沮丧而不是富有成效？这样一来，消极的情绪就可能给你们为建立共同理解所作的努力蒙上一层阴影。

passages.en: In fact collaborative problem-solving conversations require skills. Strong listening skills are essential. Sprinkling in positivity via appreciation, __(27)__ smiles, and warm comments helps. So does the essential ability to keep your emotional tone in the calm zone. If the tone of a dialogue heats up and anger erupts, the dialogue __(28)__ from collaborative to adversarial, and progress is likely to come to an immediate __(29)__ .
passages.zh: 事实上，协作式的问题解决对话需要一定的技巧。良好的倾听能力至关重要。通过表达欣赏、亲切地微笑以及说些温暖的话语来增添积极氛围，会有所帮助。同样重要的还有保持情绪基调平和的能力。如果对话的语气升温并爆发愤怒，这场对话就会从协作转变为对抗，进展很可能会立即停止。

passages.en: In addition, effective dialogue generally has another important characteristic: symmetry.
passages.zh: 此外，有效的对话通常还具有另一个重要特征：对称性。

passages.en: Symmetry in dialogue refers to the balance of how much each partner talks. Are you each getting equal airtime? When one participant does most of the talking, this asymmetry or lack of balance tends to become annoying to one or both of you. The silent partner __(30)__ tires of only listening, while the talker can feel __(31)__ . Usually, both would prefer more equal give and take.
passages.zh: 对话中的对称性，是指双方发言多少的平衡。你们是否都获得了相等的发言时间？当一方占据了大部分发言时间时，这种不对称或缺乏平衡的状态往往会令一方或双方感到恼人。沉默的一方通常会因只能倾听而感到疲倦，而多说话的一方则可能觉得负担过重。通常，双方都会希望有更多平等的交流和互动。

passages.en: Different rates of speech and levels of voice volume can __(32)__ symmetry as well. The faster or louder partner can easily begin taking up more airtime. The slower-talking or softer-voiced one can have trouble getting the floor.
passages.zh: 不同的语速和音量大小也会破坏这种对称性。说话更快或声音更大的一方很容易开始占据更多的发言时间。说话较慢或声音较轻的一方则可能难以获得发言机会。

passages.en: Conversations also lose balance when one partner's opinions count more than the other's. One person's input may carry more sway because their style of expression is more __(33)__ . One viewpoint may tend to get lost because it is expressed more __(34)__ .
passages.zh: 当一方的意见比另一方的意见更受重视时，对话也会失去平衡。一个人的表达方式可能更有气势，因此其意见更具影响力。某种观点则可能因为表达得更加谨慎而容易被忽视。

passages.en: If either partner fairly consistently __(35)__ or evaporates, modifying the pattern will be helpful. The dialogue will feel more productive, and at the same time, the relationship overall is likely to feel more positive.
passages.zh: 如果双方中的任何一方长期处于主导地位，或几乎不参与对话，改变这种模式都会有所帮助。对话会让人感觉更有成效，同时，双方的整体关系也很可能会变得更加积极。

wordbank.gloss: 受宠若惊的；奉承（过去式/过去分词）
负担过重的；使负担过重

rows.text: L) shadow名词
「cast a ___ over」固定搭配，宾语位 → 名词
cast a shadow over——投下阴影的固定隐喻 shadow 与 cast ... over 构成 cast a shadow over（给某事投下阴霾），形象表达 Negative energy（消极情绪）笼罩 efforts to build a shared understanding（构建共识的努力），地道贴切。
K)scenariocast a scenario 不成话 scenario 表「设想情景」，英语中没有 cast a scenario over 的用法；且消极情绪「投下一个情景」逻辑也不通。
A) affectionate形容词
并列名词前的修饰位 → 形容词
亲切的微笑，与 warm comments 同色 affectionate 意为「亲切、充满感情的」，修饰 smiles 是高频搭配（affectionate smile/look），与并列项 warm comments 共同构成积极正能量信号，正切「Sprinkling in positivity」主旨。

E)flattered对象错位：人才会 flattered，微笑本身不会 flattered 描述「（人）受宠若惊的」，修饰 smiles 语义不通——是「人对微笑感到受宠若惊」，而非「flattered smiles」。 H)overburdened感情色彩相反 overburdened 意为「负担过重的」，是消极色，与「Sprinkling in positivity」整段正向氛围冲突。 O)vigorous搭配不当：强烈的微笑不地道 vigorous 意为「强有力的、激烈的」，常修饰 exercise/debate，不修饰 smiles；且与温柔的 warm comments 不同色。此处先留作下文 33 题候选。
F) flips动词
主句缺谓语，单数主语 → 动词单三
flip from X to Y——突然翻转 flips 表「（状态）突然翻转」，正好对应 from collaborative to adversarial（从协作翻成对抗）；与上文 anger erupts（怒气爆发）的「突变」语气吻合。
C)elapseselapse 只用于「时间流逝」 elapses 仅与 time/hours/days 搭配表「时间过去」，不接 from...to... 表对话「转变」。 I)predominates「占主导」无 from...to... 用法 predominates 意为「占上风」，是状态而非转变，搭配 from...to... 语义不通。留作 35 题候选。
G) halt名词
「come to a/an ___」固定搭配，宾语位 → 名词
come to a halt——立即中止的惯用表达 halt 与 come to 构成英语高频搭配 come to a halt（戛然而止）。前文说「dialogue flips from collaborative to adversarial」，对话转入对抗后，「progress is likely to come to an immediate halt」逻辑顺畅。
K)scenario「come to a scenario」搭配不存在 scenario 意为「设想情景」，英语里没有 come to a scenario 这种用法；且 scenario 强调「场景设想」，与「progress（进展）」的归宿不搭。
N) typically副词
主谓之间插入副词修饰动词
陈述常态规律 → 通常 本段在讲「不对称话量带来的常见后果」，是一个一般性规律陈述；typically 正好表示「通常情况下沉默的一方听久了会厌倦」，与下半句 while the talker can feel __(31)__ 的常态描述对仗。
B)approximately「大约」用于数量，不修饰动词常态 approximately 主要用于数字/数量前（approximately 100 people），不用在主谓之间表频度。 M)tentatively「试探地」与「厌倦」逻辑不搭 tentatively 表「犹豫地、试探地」，搭 tires of listening 语义不通——人不会「试探地厌倦」。留作 34 题候选。
H) overburdened形容词
feel 后接表语 → 形容词
讲个不停的人会感到「负担过重」 上半句 The silent partner typically tires of only listening, 是沉默方的负面感受；while 形成对照，话多方一直独挑话题，自然 overburdened（不堪重负）——与下句 Usually, both would prefer more equal give and take. 「希望更对等」呼应。
E)flattered感情色彩反了：受宠若惊与抱怨不对 flattered 是积极感受「受宠若惊」，但下句明确说「双方都希望更对等的 give and take」，说明话多方是不满，色彩相反。 O)vigorousvigorous 不修饰「感觉」 vigorous 修饰人或活动表「精力充沛」，但 feel vigorous 与上下文「话题不平衡的烦恼」不搭。留作 33 题候选。
最具迷惑性的错误词是 E) —— feel 后形容词位 → 容易误选 flattered。词性匹配、又似乎「话多的一方受人追捧」逻辑也讲得通，极具迷惑性。防坑：往下读一句 Usually, both would prefer more equal give and take.——既然双方都希望更对等，说明话多方也在抱怨，必为负面感受，overburdened 才对。
D) erode动词
情态动词 can 后接动词原形
侵蚀对称——负向破坏 erode 表「逐渐侵蚀、削弱」，宾语 symmetry 正好被「侵蚀」；下文 The faster or louder partner can easily begin taking up more airtime. 印证：语速/音量差异会逐渐打破平衡。
J)propagate「传播对称」方向反了 propagate 意为「传播、繁殖」，是正向扩散，与本段「打破对称」的负向逻辑相反。
O) vigorous形容词
more + 空 — 形容词比较级位
更铿锵有力的表达风格 vigorous 修饰 style of expression 表「铿锵有力、强势」，与 One person's input may carry more sway（更具影响力）形成因果——表达风格更有力，因此话语权更大。
E)flattered受宠若惊的表达不通 flattered 描述人的情绪「受宠若惊」，不能修饰 style of expression；且语义与「话语权更大」无因果关联。
M) tentatively副词
more + 空，修饰动词 expressed → 副词
试探性地表达 → 容易被忽视 tentatively 表「试探性地、犹豫地」，与上文 vigorous（强有力）形成鲜明对照：一方表达强势，另一方表达试探——所以 One viewpoint may tend to get lost（观点被忽视）。
B)approximatelyapproximately 用于数量，不修饰表达方式 approximately 表「大约、近似」，搭配数字/数量；说话「大约地表达」不通，也无法解释观点为何「被忽视」。
最具迷惑性的错误词是 B) —— 副词位 → 容易误选 approximately。看到 more + 空就抓副词，approximately 是副词没错，但它只搭数字。防坑：把 expressed more approximately 整句读出来——「更近似地表达」逻辑上无法解释「观点被忽视」，反义对照才合理，tentatively 才是答案。
I) predominates动词
if 从句缺谓语，单数主语 → 动词单三
占主导 vs 隐没——本段对照的两极 predominates 表「占主导、压过另一方」，与并列项 evaporates（消失、隐没）正好是一对反义对照：一方持续占上风、另一方消失，呼应前文「话量不对称」的整体主题。

longreading.title: 2024年12月·第2套 英语六级长篇阅读（信息匹配） 第 1 篇 · 36–45 题答案与解析

passages.en: A) Blue moons, rose moons, supermoons. For some reason all the websites seem to think you really want to know all about these moons. "Catch This Weekend's AMAZING SUPERMOON," one headline will announce. "The Supermoon Isn't Actually A Big Deal And You're All Ruining Astronomy," another will complain.
passages.zh: 蓝月、玫瑰月、超级月亮。不知为何，所有网站似乎都认为你真的很想了解这些月亮的一切。一则标题会宣布：“捕捉本周末令人惊叹的超级月亮！”另一则标题则会抱怨：“超级月亮其实没什么大不了的，而你们全都在毁掉天文学。”

passages.en: B) The latest example is the super blood wolf moon eclipse which sounds like the name of an emotional song I would have performed a modern dance routine to in 9th grade, but is, in fact, an astronomical event set to occur on January 20. As we'll explain below, there is nothing truly mysterious or otherwise special about this moon, and it will not look like a bloody wolf head in the sky or anything wild like that. We get these super lunar events by smashing together all the qualifiers we've historically used to keep track of full moons throughout the year, and in the age of the internet we can get a little too enthusiastic.
passages.zh: 最近的例子是超级血狼月食，这听起来像一首情感歌曲的名字，我在九年级时可能会伴着它表演一段现代舞，但实际上，它是一场定于1月20日发生的天文事件。正如我们将在下文解释的那样，这轮月亮并没有什么真正神秘或特别之处，它不会在天空中呈现出血淋淋的狼头，也不会出现任何类似的狂野景象。我们所谓的这些超级月球事件，是把历史上用来记录全年满月的所有限定词拼凑在一起的结果，而在互联网时代，我们有时会对此过于兴奋。

passages.en: C) Consider this your go-to resource for all moon-gazing news. Here's what you need to know about the latest lunar event.
passages.zh: 把这篇文章当作你获取所有观月新闻的首选资料吧。以下是你需要了解的最新月球事件。

passages.en: D) Look, it's okay if you don't know. There are probably loads of folks who walk around pretending they totally know why that thing in the sky seems to get bigger and smaller at regular intervals but who totally do not.
passages.zh: 听着，不知道也没关系。可能有很多人整天装作自己完全知道为什么天空中的那个东西似乎会以固定的时间间隔变大变小，但实际上他们根本不知道。

passages.en: E) The moon orbits Earth, and it's tidally locked—that means it always shows us the same face, instead of spinning around like our planet does. That's why you can always see the man on the moon (or the moon rabbit, depending on your cultural preferences) even as it spins around us. But while the moon is big and bright in the sky when it's full, that's only because it's reflecting light from the sun. But the moon is always moving, so it's getting hit with sunlight at different angles. It's invisible to us during the new moon, because our satellite is parked right between us and the sun; the so-called dark side of the moon is lit up like Las Vegas, but the side we can see is in shadow. A full moon happens when the earth is right between the sun and the moon, so sunlight hits the part we can see. And all the other phases are just the transition from one of those extremes to the other.
passages.zh: 月球绕地球运行，而且它与地球处于潮汐锁定状态——这意味着它始终以同一面朝向我们，而不像我们的星球那样自转。因此，即使月球绕着我们旋转，你也总能看到月亮上的人脸（或者月兔，取决于你的文化偏好）。不过，月亮在满月时之所以在天空中又大又亮，只是因为它反射了太阳光。月球始终在运动，所以它受到阳光照射的角度也在不断变化。新月期间我们看不见它，因为这颗卫星正好停在我们和太阳之间；所谓月球的暗面其实被照得像拉斯维加斯一样明亮，但我们能看到的那一面处于阴影中。满月发生时，地球正好位于太阳和月球之间，因此阳光照亮了我们能看到的那一面。其他所有月相，都只是从这两个极端状态过渡到另一个极端状态的过程。

passages.en: F) The moon isn't always exactly the same distance from Earth, because its orbit isn't perfectly circular. We call the closest point perigee(近地点), and the most distant point is apogee(远地点). 2018's closest perigee and most distant apogee both happened in January, and the difference was about 30,000 miles.
passages.zh: 月球与地球的距离并不总是完全相同，因为它的轨道并非完美的圆形。我们把最近的点称为近地点，把最远的点称为远地点。2018年，月球距离地球最近的近地点和最远的远地点都发生在1月，两者相差约3万英里。

passages.en: G) The reason you care about this ordinary change in distance is that it turns a moon super. When a full moon happens close to perigee, it's going to look a bit bigger. Honestly, the difference is not that profound, but if you're in a position to photograph the supermoon next to something that shows the slight increase in scale, it can look pretty cool. January's super blood wolf moon eclipse is super because the date lines up with the closest the moon will get to us during January, but the moon won't actually be at its closest for the year until February's supermoon, which you can expect plenty of undue excitement over.
passages.zh: 你之所以会在意这种普通的距离变化，是因为它会让月亮变成“超级月亮”。当满月发生在接近近地点的位置时，它看起来会大一些。老实说，这种差异并不十分明显，但如果你能把超级月亮和某个能够显示其尺寸略有增加的物体拍在一起，效果还是相当酷的。1月的超级血狼月食之所以是“超级”的，是因为它发生的日期与月球在1月距离我们最近的时间相吻合，但月球要到2月的超级月亮时才会达到全年最近的位置，而届时你可以预料到人们会对此产生大量不必要的兴奋。

passages.en: H) Blood moons only occur during total lunar eclipses (which can happen a few times a year in any given location). When the moon slips through our shadow, we give it a reddish coloring. The moon can also look orange whenever it's rising or setting, or if it hangs low in the horizon all night—the light bouncing off of it has to travel through a thicker atmosphere there, which scatters more blue light away. But you'll probably only see that deep, sinister red during an eclipse.
passages.zh: 血月只会出现在月全食期间（月全食在任何特定地点每年可能发生几次）。当月球穿过我们的影子时，我们会看到它呈现红色。月亮在升起或落下时也可能呈橙色，或者如果它整晚都低悬在地平线附近，也会呈现这种颜色——在那里，月光必须穿过更厚的大气层，大气会散射掉更多的蓝光。不过，你可能只有在月食期间才能看到那种深沉而诡异的红色。

passages.en: I) A lot of headlines about moons are just ridiculous (you do not need to be particularly excited about a blue moon, it just looks like a regular full moon), but you should definitely roll out of bed to look at a blood moon if one is going to be visible in your region, even though they're just lunar eclipses and not evidence of bloody battles between the sky gods.
passages.zh: 许多关于月亮的标题都十分荒谬（你没必要因为蓝月而特别兴奋，它看起来就像普通的满月），但如果某次血月将在你所在的地区出现，你绝对应该从床上爬起来看看，尽管它们不过是月食，并不能证明天空之神之间曾发生过血腥的战斗。

passages.en: J) In March of 2018, we had our second "blue moon" of the year, to much acclaim. And while that's not necessarily special in an oh-gosh-get-out-and-look-at-it way, it's certainly special: a blue moon is a nickname for when two full moons fall in the same calendar month, and we hadn't previously had two in one year since 1999. We won't have it happen again until 2037. Astronomer David Chapman explained that this is merely a peculiarity of our calendar; once we stopped doing things based on the moon and started trying to follow the sun and the seasons, we stopped having one reliable full moon per month. The moon cycle is 29.53 days long on average, so in most months we still end up with a single new moon and a single full one. But every once in a while, one month steals a full moon from another. In 2018 (and in 1999, and again in 2037) both January and March stacked full moons on the first and last nights of the month, leaving February in the dark.
passages.zh: 2018年3月，我们迎来了当年的第二次“蓝月”，受到了一片赞誉。虽然从“天哪，快出去看看”的角度来说，它未必有什么特别之处，但它确实很特别：蓝月是一个昵称，指的是同一个公历月份出现两次满月的情况，而在此之前，我们上一次在同一年中出现两次蓝月还是1999年。下一次要等到2037年。天文学家戴维·查普曼解释说，这只不过是我们的日历造成的一种特殊现象；当我们不再根据月亮安排事情，转而试图遵循太阳和季节的规律后，就不再每月都有一个可靠的满月了。月球周期平均为29.53天，因此大多数月份仍然会出现一次新月和一次满月。但偶尔会有一个月从另一个月那里“偷走”一次满月。在2018年（以及1999年和2037年），1月和3月都在当月的第一晚和最后一晚出现了满月，结果让2月陷入了黑暗。

passages.en: K) Getting two blue moons a year is rare, but we have individual blue moons every few years. Also, fun fact: not actually blue. A moon can indeed take on a moody blue color, but this only happens when particles of just the right size disperse through the sky—and it has nothing to do with the moon's status as "blue". Big clouds of ash from volcanic eruptions or fires can do the trick, but it doesn't happen often, and the stars would certainly have to align for two such rare instances to occur at once.
passages.zh: 一年中出现两次蓝月很罕见，但我们每隔几年还是会遇到一次蓝月。此外，还有一个有趣的事实：它其实并不是蓝色的。月亮确实可能呈现出忧郁的蓝色，但这只有在大小恰到好处的颗粒散布在天空中时才会发生，而且这与月亮被称为“蓝月”毫无关系。火山喷发或火灾产生的大量火山灰可以造成这种效果，但这种情况并不常见，而要让两次如此罕见的现象同时发生，当然还得碰上极其难得的巧合。

passages.en: L) You may have heard that the super special second blue moon of 2018 was also a Paschal moon. This is true! That just means it was the first full moon of spring, which is often used to determine the date of Easter Sunday. All of this is just calendar nonsense and we refuse to go into it further.
passages.zh: 你可能听说过，2018年那次超级特别的第二次蓝月同时也是复活节月。这是真的！这只意味着它是春季的第一个满月，人们通常会用它来确定复活节星期日的日期。这一切都只是日历方面的胡闹，我们拒绝再进一步讨论。

passages.en: M) Sometimes you'll see a headline that promises a moon with so many qualifiers it makes your head spin. A super blue blood worm moon, perhaps? Or a super blood wolf moon? Lots of websites will tell you that "wolf moon" is the traditional name of the first full moon of the year in "Native American" cultures, which is kind of a weird thing to claim given that there are 573 registered Tribal Nations in the US alone today, not to mention historically. The idea that hungry, howling wolves were such a universal constant in January that all of North America with its different cultures, geographies, and languages spontaneously came up with the same nickname is illogical.
passages.zh: 有时你会看到这样的标题：它给月亮加上了如此多的限定词，足以让你头晕目眩。比如“超级蓝色血月蠕虫月”？或者“超级血狼月”？许多网站会告诉你，“狼月”是“美洲原住民”文化中对一年中第一次满月的传统称呼。鉴于仅美国如今就有573个登记在册的部落民族，更不用说历史上的情况了，这种说法多少有些奇怪。认为饥饿并嚎叫的狼在1月如此普遍，以至于整个北美洲不同的文化、地理环境和语言都自发地创造出了同一个昵称，这种想法并不合乎逻辑。

passages.en: N) Many cultures have traditional names for the full moon in a given month or season, so there's quite a list to draw from if you're trying to really juice up a story on a slightly-bigger-than-average view of the moon. But these are all based on human calendars and activities and folklore; you will not go outside and see a pink moon in April, though I wish it were so.
passages.zh: 许多文化都为特定月份或季节的满月保留着传统名称，所以如果你想为一轮比平均大小略大的月亮大肆渲染一番故事，可以从中列出很长的清单。但这些名称全都建立在人类的日历、活动和民间传说之上；你不会在4月走到户外就看到一轮粉红月，尽管我真希望那是真的。

statements.en: We cannot see the moon at times when it is positioned right between the earth and the sun.
statements.zh: 当月球正好位于地球和太阳之间时,我们看不到月球。

analysis.锚点: 月亮卡在地日之间不可见
analysis.定位: E 段 It's invisible to us during the new moon, because our satellite is parked right between us and the sun; the so-called dark side of the moon is lit up like Las Vegas, but the side we can see is in shadow. 新月时月亮对我们是不可见的，因为我们的卫星正停在我们和太阳之间；月球所谓的“暗面”被照得像拉斯维加斯一样亮，而我们能看到的那一面则处在阴影中。
analysis.改写: We cannot see the moon↔It's invisible to us 看不见 = 不可见 when it is positioned right between the earth and the sun↔our satellite is parked right between us and the sun 位于=停在，月=卫星

statements.en: Volcanic eruptions may cause the moon to assume a moody blue color.
statements.zh: 火山爆发可能导致月球呈现出忧郁的蓝色。

analysis.锚点: 火山喷发与忧郁蓝色月亮
analysis.定位: K 段 A moon can indeed take on a moody blue color, but this only happens when particles of just the right size disperse through the sky—and it has nothing to do with the moon's status as "blue". Big clouds of ash from volcanic eruptions or fires can do the trick, but it doesn't happen often, and the stars would certainly have to align for two such rare instances to occur at once. 月亮确实可以呈现一种忧郁的蓝色，但这种情况只发生在合适尺寸的颗粒在天空中扩散的时候——和月亮的“蓝月”身份毫无关系。火山爆发或火灾产生的大片灰云能做到这一点，但这种情况并不常发生，要两件如此罕见的事同时出现真得天时地利人和。
analysis.改写: Volcanic eruptions↔Big clouds of ash from volcanic eruptions or fires 术语原样复现 may cause the moon to assume a moody blue color↔can do the trick 动词短语承接前句指代

statements.en: The moon will be closest to the earth when the supermoon occurs in February.
statements.zh: 二月份出现超级月亮时,月球将距离地球最近。

analysis.定位: G 段 January's super blood wolf moon eclipse is super because the date lines up with the closest the moon will get to us during January, but the moon won't actually be at its closest for the year until February's supermoon, which you can expect plenty of undue excitement over. 1 月的超级血狼月食之所以“超级”，是因为日期对上了月亮在 1 月里离我们最近的时刻，但月亮要到 2 月的超级月亮时才真正达到全年最近的距离，到时你又能预期一波过度的兴奋。
analysis.改写: The moon will be closest to the earth↔the moon won't actually be at its closest for the year not until=才 的逻辑反转 when the supermoon occurs in February↔February's supermoon 名词所属结构 → 时间从句
analysis.辨邻: F F 段 2018's closest perigee and most distant apogee both happened in January 把最近距离锁在 1 月，与陈述句要的“2 月最近”恰好相反；F 段是话题相邻段（都讲距离），但并没有承载本句信息。 2018's closest perigee and most distant apogee both happened in January

statements.en: There is nothing unusual about the super blood wolf moon, which will bear no resemblance to a bloody wolf head.
statements.zh: 超级血狼月并无任何异常之处,它不会与血淋淋的狼头有任何相似之处。

analysis.锚点: 超级血狼月与血淋狼头
analysis.定位: B 段 As we'll explain below, there is nothing truly mysterious or otherwise special about this moon, and it will not look like a bloody wolf head in the sky or anything wild like that. 我们下面会解释，关于这个月亮其实没有任何真正神秘或特别之处，它也不会在天上看起来像一个血淋淋的狼头或别的什么疯狂的样子。
analysis.改写: There is nothing unusual about the super blood wolf moon↔there is nothing truly mysterious or otherwise special about this moon unusual=mysterious or special which will bear no resemblance to a bloody wolf head↔it will not look like a bloody wolf head in the sky bear no resemblance to=will not look like

statements.en: The moon will appear orange when the light reflecting from it travels through an atmosphere thicker than usual.
statements.zh: 当从月球反射的光线穿过比平常更厚的大气层时,月球将呈现橙色。

analysis.定位: H 段 The moon can also look orange whenever it's rising or setting, or if it hangs low in the horizon all night—the light bouncing off of it has to travel through a thicker atmosphere there, which scatters more blue light away. 月亮在升起或落下时，或者整夜挂在地平线附近时，也会看上去呈橙色——因为从它反射出去的光必须穿过那里更厚的大气层，而较厚的大气层会把更多的蓝光散射掉。
analysis.改写: The moon will appear orange↔The moon can also look orange appear=look when the light reflecting from it travels through an atmosphere thicker than usual↔the light bouncing off of it has to travel through a thicker atmosphere there reflecting=bouncing off, thicker than usual=thicker

statements.en: It is contrary to logic to claim the name of wolf moon originates from the cultures of American Indians.
statements.zh: 声称狼月这个名称起源于美洲印第安人的文化是不合逻辑的。

analysis.锚点: 狼月名字源自美洲印第安
analysis.定位: M 段 Lots of websites will tell you that "wolf moon" is the traditional name of the first full moon of the year in "Native American" cultures, which is kind of a weird thing to claim given that there are 573 registered Tribal Nations in the US alone today, not to mention historically. The idea that hungry, howling wolves were such a universal constant in January that all of North America with its different cultures, geographies, and languages spontaneously came up with the same nickname is illogical. 很多网站会告诉你“狼月”是“美洲原住民”文化中一年第一次满月的传统名字，但这种说法挺奇怪——光今日美国就有 573 个注册部落，更别提历史上的部落了。“饥饿、嗥叫的狼”在 1 月是这样一种放之北美而皆准的常量，以至于不同文化、地理、语言的整个北美都自发想出同一昵称——这种说法不合逻辑。
analysis.改写: It is contrary to logic to claim↔is illogical contrary to logic=illogical the name of wolf moon originates from the cultures of American Indians↔“wolf moon” is the traditional name of the first full moon of the year in “Native American” cultures American Indians = Native American

statements.en: As the moon's orbit is not a hundred-percent circle, its distance from the earth changes.
statements.zh: 由于月球的轨道不是百分之百的圆形,它与地球的距离会发生变化。

analysis.定位: F 段 The moon isn't always exactly the same distance from Earth, because its orbit isn't perfectly circular. 月亮和地球的距离并不总是一模一样，因为它的轨道并非完全是圆形。
analysis.改写: the moon's orbit is not a hundred-percent circle↔its orbit isn't perfectly circular hundred-percent=perfectly its distance from the earth changes↔The moon isn't always exactly the same distance from Earth 距离变化 = 距离不总相同

statements.en: A full moon in a given month or season gets a specific name in different cultures.
statements.zh: 在不同文化中,特定月份或季节的满月会有特定的名称。

analysis.锚点: 不同文化给某月满月起名
analysis.定位: N 段 Many cultures have traditional names for the full moon in a given month or season, so there's quite a list to draw from if you're trying to really juice up a story on a slightly-bigger-than-average view of the moon. 许多文化对特定月份或季节的满月都有传统名字，所以如果你想给一篇关于“略大于平均”的月亮观感的报道加点料，可选的名字相当多。
analysis.改写: A full moon in a given month or season↔the full moon in a given month or season 限定结构原样复现 gets a specific name in different cultures↔Many cultures have traditional names for 主谓换序的等价改写
analysis.辨邻: M M 段 wolf moon 是单一例子的反例，并非总括“许多文化对某月/某季满月起名”这条事实；总括段是 N。 “wolf moon” is the traditional name of the first full moon of the year in “Native American” cultures

statements.en: There are likely lots of people who know absolutely nothing about why the moon appears to change its size regularly but act like they know.
statements.zh: 很可能有很多人对月球为何看起来会定期改变大小一无所知,却表现得好像他们知道。

analysis.定位: D 段 There are probably loads of folks who walk around pretending they totally know why that thing in the sky seems to get bigger and smaller at regular intervals but who totally do not. 可能有一大堆人到处走来走去，假装自己完全知道天上那玩意儿为什么看上去会有规律地变大变小，但其实完全不知道。
analysis.改写: lots of people who know absolutely nothing↔loads of folks who walk around pretending they totally know...but who totally do not lots=loads, people=folks why the moon appears to change its size regularly↔why that thing in the sky seems to get bigger and smaller at regular intervals the moon=that thing in the sky act like they know↔pretending they totally know act like=pretend
analysis.辨邻: E E 段是科学解释段，回答“月相为何变化”，但本句要的是 act like they know 这条人物画像——E 段没有装懂者的描写。 And all the other phases are just the transition from one of those extremes to the other

statements.en: When a full moon appears twice in the same month, it is nicknamed a blue moon.
statements.zh: 当同一个月内出现两次满月时,它被称为蓝月亮。

analysis.定位: J 段 And while that's not necessarily special in an oh-gosh-get-out-and-look-at-it way, it's certainly special: a blue moon is a nickname for when two full moons fall in the same calendar month, and we hadn't previously had two in one year since 1999. 尽管这并不属于“哦天哪赶紧出门看”那种特别，但它确实算特别：蓝月是给“同一个日历月里出现两次满月”这种情况起的昵称，而我们上一次在一年里出现两次蓝月还是 1999 年。
analysis.改写: When a full moon appears twice in the same month↔when two full moons fall in the same calendar month 数词分布的等价改写 it is nicknamed a blue moon↔a blue moon is a nickname for 定义方向反转
analysis.辨邻: K K 段 not actually blue 与 moody blue color 都谈“蓝月颜色”，并不给“蓝月”的命名定义；定义段是 J。 Also, fun fact: not actually blue

reading1.title: 2024年12月·第2套 英语六级阅读理解（四选一） 第 1 篇 · 46–50 题答案与解析

passages.en: With population increases and global urbanisation ever accelerating, much attention is focused on the sustainability of our cities and scarce attention is paid to the countryside.
passages.zh: 随着人口增长和全球城市化进程不断加快，人们越来越关注城市的可持续性，而对乡村的关注却十分有限。

passages.en: Rural life is associated with closely-knit communities, sense of belonging, and a simple, tranquil life. Yet whilst some or all of these elements exist in the countryside, so do conservatism and a lack of employment opportunities. And it is mostly due to the latter that rural communities are suffering. Attracted by the improved economics of urban areas, country-dwellers across the world are moving out, contributing to the excessive crowdedness of densely populated cities, and leaving the countryside in desolation.
passages.zh: 乡村生活与紧密团结的社区、归属感以及简单宁静的生活联系在一起。然而，尽管乡村存在其中一些或全部要素，保守主义和就业机会匮乏也同样存在。乡村社区之所以正在遭受困境，主要是由于后者。受到城市地区更好经济条件的吸引，世界各地的乡村居民纷纷外迁，加剧了人口稠密城市的过度拥挤，也使乡村陷入荒凉。

passages.en: So how can the countryside ensure its survival among these changes; or should it at all? Due to both the distance between residences and facilities and often intermittent public transport, those living in the countryside are heavier automobile users. Rural dwellers also use more energy maintaining their mostly detached buildings. We may be piled up like boxes in the city, but this brings energy efficiency that the countryside cannot match. Rural energy requirements result in higher carbon emissions per person than in the city, so it is actually irresponsible to endorse such a lifestyle choice.
passages.zh: 那么，在这些变化中，乡村应如何确保自身的生存；或者说，它是否根本就应该继续存在？由于住宅与公共设施之间距离较远，而且公共交通往往时断时续，乡村居民更加依赖汽车。乡村居民在维护大多为独立式的住宅建筑时也会消耗更多能源。我们在城市里或许像箱子一样拥挤地堆叠在一起，但这带来了乡村无法匹敌的能源效率。乡村的能源需求导致其人均碳排放量高于城市，因此，支持这种生活方式选择实际上是不负责任的。

passages.en: Protecting the countryside is a hot topic. Those who have made their fortunes in the city often buy second homes in the countryside, visiting intermittently for a sample of a supposedly simple life. The side-effect of this is that house prices are pushed up due to increased demand, leaving them unaffordable for local people. A solution has yet to be found for this challenge, for market forces are further forcing residents out of the countryside. For those who believe in rural preservation, this is deplorable.
passages.zh: 保护乡村是一个热门话题。那些在城市中发家致富的人常常在乡村购买第二套住房，间歇性地前往那里，体验所谓简单生活的一小部分。其副作用是，需求增加推高了房价，使当地居民无力承担。这个挑战至今仍未找到解决办法，因为市场力量正进一步迫使居民离开乡村。对于那些相信应保护乡村的人来说，这是令人痛心的。

passages.en: Whilst an idealised view of the countryside is common, the reality is that rural life has continuously evolved. Industrialisation brought an increase in divisions of labour, changing social links between rural people. The internet has introduced once foreign cultures into the countryside. Improved travel connections and affordability have made the world more accessible, creating a "global village". Considering these changes, surely an evolving countryside is inevitable.
passages.zh: 尽管人们普遍对乡村抱有理想化的看法，但事实是，乡村生活一直在不断演变。工业化带来了劳动分工的增加，改变了乡村居民之间的社会联系。互联网将曾经陌生的文化带入了乡村。交通联系的改善以及出行成本的降低使世界变得更加触手可及，创造了一个“地球村”。考虑到这些变化，一个不断发展的乡村必然是不可避免的。

passages.en: Perhaps the countryside should also prepare itself for massive population increases in the future. With cities across the world growing rapidly, how will the current urban generation respond to the inevitable social changes of mass urbanisation? Will the longing for a simpler life become stronger, fueling a rural renaissance?
passages.zh: 或许乡村也应为未来人口的大幅增长做好准备。随着世界各地的城市迅速发展，当前这一代城市居民将如何应对大规模城市化必然带来的社会变化？对更简单生活的向往是否会变得更加强烈，从而推动乡村复兴？

passages.en: As the world continues to urbanise, the voices calling for rural preservation may well grow louder. But change is inevitable. We know that the world is going to see new cities emerging from the dust and current cities growing into megacities, but the future of the countryside is less clear.
passages.zh: 随着世界继续城市化，呼吁保护乡村的声音很可能会越来越响亮。但变化是不可避免的。我们知道，未来世界将会有新的城市从尘埃中崛起，现有城市也将发展成为特大城市，但乡村的未来则不那么明朗。

questions.stem: What has become of the rural areas nowadays?
questions.stem_zh: 如今农村地区变成了什么样子?

options.text: They are becoming somewhat deserted.
options.zh: 它们正在变得有些荒凉。

options.text: They are being increasingly urbanised.
options.zh: 它们正在日益城市化。

options.text: They are closely-knit communities.

questions.判型: What has become of the rural areas nowadays? 问的是「现在乡村怎么样了」，要的是客观状态描述，不含 infer/suggest/imply。
questions.拆句: What has become of the rural areas nowadays? 是常规疑问句，become of 是固定搭配，意为「（某事物）变成了什么样、下场如何」，整句直译为「乡村现在变成什么样了」，无陷阱。
questions.定位: P2 Attracted by the improved economics of urban areas, country-dwellers across the world are moving out, contributing to the excessive crowdedness of densely populated cities, and leaving the countryside in desolation. 受城市改善的经济条件吸引，世界各地的乡村居民正在外迁，加剧了人口稠密城市的过度拥挤，并使乡村陷入荒凉。

locate.en: Attracted by the improved economics of urban areas, country-dwellers across the world are moving out, contributing to the excessive crowdedness of densely populated cities, and leaving the countryside in desolation.
locate.zh: 受城市改善的经济条件吸引，世界各地的乡村居民正在外迁，加剧了人口稠密城市的过度拥挤，并使乡村陷入荒凉。

option_analysis.note: A 把「正在外流→正变得荒凉」浓缩成 becoming somewhat deserted，与预判完全一致；somewhat 还为「程度词」留了余地，避免被「过于绝对」反驳。

pairs.orig: country-dwellers across the world are moving out

option_analysis.note: 原文讲的是 contributing to the excessive crowdedness of densely populated cities——人去了城市，乡村反而空了；选项 They are being increasingly urbanised. 却说乡村正被「城市化」，方向完全相反。
Rural life is associated with closely-knit communities 说的是乡村生活「被联想为」紧密社区，是一种「印象」，并非 nowadays 的现实；选项 They are closely-knit communities. 把印象当现状。
so do conservatism and a lack of employment opportunities 把 conservatism 与「就业不足」并列为问题，原文紧接着说 And it is mostly due to the latter that rural communities are suffering——主因是后者（就业），并非保守主义；D 把次要因素夸大为现状。

questions.stem: What does the author think of the rural lifestyle?
questions.stem_zh: 作者如何看待农村生活方式?

options.text: It is unlikely to survive given the on-going changes.
options.zh: 鉴于持续的变化,它不太可能存续下去。

options.text: It is less energy-efficient compared to that in cities.
options.zh: 与城市生活方式相比,它的能源效率较低。

options.text: It is highly dependent upon heavy automobiles.
options.zh: 它高度依赖重型汽车。

options.text: It is a choice more affluent people will endorse.
options.zh: 它是更富裕的人会认可的选择。

questions.判型: What does the author think of the rural lifestyle? 问作者对乡村生活方式的明确观点，答案是原文直接写出的评价，并未要求做逻辑推断。
questions.拆句: What does the author think of the rural lifestyle? 是固定句型，think of=「对……的看法」；直译「作者怎么看乡村生活方式」，无陷阱。
questions.定位: P3 We may be piled up like boxes in the city, but this brings energy efficiency that the countryside cannot match. Rural energy requirements result in higher carbon emissions per person than in the city, so it is actually irresponsible to endorse such a lifestyle choice. 我们在城市里也许像盒子一样堆在一起，但这带来了乡村无法企及的能效。乡村的能耗导致人均碳排比城市更高，因此推崇这种生活方式实际上是不负责任的。

locate.en: We may be piled up like boxes in the city, but this brings energy efficiency that the countryside cannot match. Rural energy requirements result in higher carbon emissions per person than in the city, so it is actually irresponsible to endorse such a lifestyle choice.
locate.zh: 我们在城市里也许像盒子一样堆在一起，但这带来了乡村无法企及的能效。乡村的能耗导致人均碳排比城市更高，因此推崇这种生活方式实际上是不负责任的。

option_analysis.note: P3 评价乡村生活方式不可取，但并未说它「无法存活」；It is unlikely to survive given the on-going changes. 借用了 how can the countryside ensure its survival 里的 survival，却把「能否生存」的话题误植到「作者对生活方式的判断」上。
整段评价的核心证据就是「乡村能效低、碳排高」，B 一字不差地复述了这层比较关系，且严格限定在「能效」维度，与预判一致。

pairs.orig: this brings energy efficiency that the countryside cannot match
pairs.opt: It is less energy-efficient compared to that in cities.

pairs.orig: higher carbon emissions per person than in the city
pairs.opt: It is less energy-efficient compared to that in cities.

option_analysis.note: those living in the countryside are heavier automobile users 说的是「乡村人是更重度的汽车使用者」（使用频率/比例更高），选项 It is highly dependent upon heavy automobiles. 把 heavier 移植到 automobiles 之前，变成「依赖重型汽车」，偷换了 heavier 的修饰对象。
原文 it is actually irresponsible to endorse such a lifestyle choice 直接评价「推崇这种生活方式是不负责任的」，作者持反对态度；选项 It is a choice more affluent people will endorse. 不仅没指出作者的反对，反而把「有钱人会推崇」当成结论。

questions.stem: What does the author think of rich urban residents buying a second home in the countryside?
questions.stem_zh: 作者如何看待富裕的城市居民在农村购买第二套住房?

options.text: It is bound to mar the traditional rural life.
options.zh: 这必然会破坏传统的农村生活。

options.text: It adversely impacts rural social stability.
options.zh: 这对农村社会稳定产生不利影响。

options.text: It hinders rural economies' revitalisation.
options.zh: 这阻碍了农村经济的复兴。

options.text: It is detrimental to rural preservation.
options.zh: 这不利于农村保护。

questions.判型: What does the author think of rich urban residents buying a second home in the countryside? 问的是作者对这一具体行为的明确评价，答案出现在原文同一段的总结句。
questions.拆句: rich urban residents buying a second home in the countryside 中 buying 是现在分词作 residents 的后置定语，相当于「买第二套乡村房的城市富人」；定语稍长但不绕。
questions.定位: P4 A solution has yet to be found for this challenge, for market forces are further forcing residents out of the countryside. For those who believe in rural preservation, this is deplorable. 这一难题尚无解决方案，因为市场力量正在进一步把居民赶出乡村。对那些信奉乡村保护的人而言，这是令人痛心的。

locate.en: A solution has yet to be found for this challenge, for market forces are further forcing residents out of the countryside. For those who believe in rural preservation, this is deplorable.
locate.zh: 这一难题尚无解决方案，因为市场力量正在进一步把居民赶出乡村。对那些信奉乡村保护的人而言，这是令人痛心的。

option_analysis.note: P4 谈的是房价与本地居民问题，并未提及 traditional rural life 是否被破坏；考生易把第二段提到的「亲密社区/简单生活」的传统印象嫁接到此，但原文未在 P4 谈这一面。
原文 house prices are pushed up... leaving them unaffordable for local people 谈的是房价与可负担性，并未谈 rural social stability；选项把经济层面问题升格成「社会稳定」这种更大的范畴。
P4 谈的是市场力量与房价，并未提及 rural economies' revitalisation；revitalisation 这一话题在 P6 rural renaissance 处才隐约出现，与 P4 的论点无关。
原文连续给出「房价上涨→本地人买不起→市场力量进一步驱赶居民→对乡村保护者而言可悲」四步推理，落脚点正是「对乡村保护不利」；D 既保留了评价的负面性，又精准落到 preservation 这个对象上。

pairs.orig: For those who believe in rural preservation, this is deplorable
pairs.opt: It is detrimental to rural preservation.

pairs.orig: leaving them unaffordable for local people
pairs.opt: It is detrimental to rural preservation.

questions.stem: What do we learn about the countryside with industrialisation and technological advances?
questions.stem_zh: 关于伴随工业化和技术进步的农村,我们了解到什么?

options.text: It is destined to change gradually.
options.zh: 它注定会逐渐改变。

options.text: It will present an idealised way of life.
options.zh: 它将呈现一种理想化的生活方式。

options.text: It is likely to embrace foreign cultures.
options.zh: 它有可能接纳外来文化。

options.text: It will become increasingly diversified.
options.zh: 它将变得日益多元化。

questions.判型: What do we learn about the countryside with industrialisation and technological advances? 问从文中得知什么，答案直接来自原文表述，不要求二步推断。
questions.拆句: the countryside with industrialisation and technological advances 中 with 引出伴随状语，意为「在工业化与技术进步的影响下」，with 短语作 countryside 的后置修饰，整句直译「在工业化与技术进步下，我们对乡村得知什么」。
questions.定位: P5 Whilst an idealised view of the countryside is common, the reality is that rural life has continuously evolved. Industrialisation brought an increase in divisions of labour, changing social links between rural people. The internet has introduced once foreign cultures into the countryside. Improved travel connections and affordability have made the world more accessible, creating a "global village". Considering these changes, surely an evolving countryside is inevitable. 尽管对乡村理想化的印象很常见，现实却是乡村生活一直在持续演变。工业化带来分工增加，改变了乡村人之间的社会联系。互联网把曾经陌生的文化带进了乡村。交通改善与可承受让世界更触手可及，造就了「地球村」。鉴于这些变化，乡村必然在演变之中。

locate.en: Whilst an idealised view of the countryside is common, the reality is that rural life has continuously evolved. Industrialisation brought an increase in divisions of labour, changing social links between rural people. The internet has introduced once foreign cultures into the countryside. Improved travel connections and affordability have made the world more accessible, creating a "global village". Considering these changes, surely an evolving countryside is inevitable.
locate.zh: 尽管对乡村理想化的印象很常见，现实却是乡村生活一直在持续演变。工业化带来分工增加，改变了乡村人之间的社会联系。互联网把曾经陌生的文化带进了乡村。交通改善与可承受让世界更触手可及，造就了「地球村」。鉴于这些变化，乡村必然在演变之中。

option_analysis.note: P5 段尾既明示必然性（inevitable）又通过 continuously evolved 暗示渐进性，A 把这两层语义都包含进 destined to change gradually，与预判完全一致。

pairs.orig: surely an evolving countryside is inevitable
pairs.opt: It is destined to change gradually.
It is destined to change gradually.

option_analysis.note: 原文 Whilst an idealised view of the countryside is common, the reality is that rural life has continuously evolved 用 whilst 让步、the reality is 转折，明确把「理想化乡村」当成被否定的印象；选项 It will present an idealised way of life. 反把它说成将要呈现的现实。
The internet has introduced once foreign cultures into the countryside 只是段中三件平行例证之一，与「分工」「全球村」共同支撑「乡村必然演变」这一论点；选项 It is likely to embrace foreign cultures. 把单一例子当成结论。
creating a "global village" 强调「世界更可及、变成地球村」，并不等于乡村会「越来越多元化」；选项 It will become increasingly diversified. 在「多文化进入」之上多走一步，推出 diversified 这个原文未说的结论。

questions.stem: What does the author think of the future of the countryside compared with cities?
questions.stem_zh: 作者如何看待农村与城市相比的未来?

options.text: It is going to be harder for the locals.
options.zh: 对于当地人来说,情况会更加艰难。

options.text: It is going to resemble that of cities.
options.zh: 它将与城市的未来相似。

options.text: It is less likely to stay static.
options.zh: 它不太可能保持静止不变。

options.text: It is less easy to envisage.
options.zh: 它更不容易设想。

questions.判型: What does the author think of the future of the countryside compared with cities? 问作者对未来的对比判断，原文末段直接给出明示对比，不需推断。
questions.拆句: What does the author think of the future of the countryside compared with cities? 中 compared with cities 是过去分词短语作 future 的后置定语，意为「与城市相比的乡村的未来」；句子结构稍长但语义直白。
questions.定位: P7 We know that the world is going to see new cities emerging from the dust and current cities growing into megacities, but the future of the countryside is less clear. 我们知道，世界将看到新城从尘土中崛起、现有城市发展为超大型城市，但乡村的未来则不那么清晰。

locate.en: We know that the world is going to see new cities emerging from the dust and current cities growing into megacities, but the future of the countryside is less clear.
locate.zh: 我们知道，世界将看到新城从尘土中崛起、现有城市发展为超大型城市，但乡村的未来则不那么清晰。

option_analysis.note: P7 未提及 harder for the locals；本地人变难的话题在 P4 leaving them unaffordable for local people 出现过，但与「未来对比」无关；选项把跨段细节挪过来冒充末段对比的结论。
原文 but the future of the countryside is less clear 把乡村未来与城市未来拉开差距；选项 It is going to resemble that of cities. 反说「乡村未来会像城市的未来」，把对比关系反转为类似关系。
But change is inevitable 谈的是变化必然，It is less likely to stay static. 复述这一变化必然性；但本题问的是「乡村未来与城市未来相比」这一对比维度，C 答的是「乡村是否会变」的另一维度。
对比型细节题正确项必须同时保留比较关系与比较内容；D 既保留 less，又把 clear 同义置换为 easy to envisage，与预判完全契合。

pairs.orig: but the future of the countryside is less clear
pairs.opt: It is less easy to envisage.

pairs.orig: We know that the world is going to see new cities emerging from the dust and current cities growing into megacities
pairs.opt: It is less easy to envisage.

reading2.title: 2024年12月·第2套 英语六级阅读理解（四选一） 第 2 篇 · 51–55 题答案与解析

passages.en: Statements, like "beauty is in the eye of the beholder(观看者)", are rarely questioned. They've become so embedded in our consciousness that people think it's absurd to think otherwise. It might be useful, however, to at least push back on this assumption because people evaluate environment, situations, and people aesthetically. We may find that we still believe it is correct, but we may also find that there is a lot more to the situation than you suppose.
passages.zh: 像“美在观看者的眼中”这样的说法很少受到质疑。它们已经如此深深地植入我们的意识，以至于人们认为持相反看法是荒谬的。然而，至少对这一假设提出质疑或许是有益的，因为人们会从审美角度评价环境、情境和他人。我们可能会发现自己仍然认为这一说法是正确的，但也可能会发现，事情远比你所设想的复杂得多。

passages.en: A recent study exploring aesthetic taste was published in Cognition. The results from this study show that people agree very much in their aesthetic evaluation of natural objects, but they disagree more about artifacts, or human-made objects.
passages.zh: 一项探讨审美趣味的最新研究发表在《认知》杂志上。该研究的结果表明，人们在对自然物体进行审美评价时具有很高的一致性，但对于人工制品，即人造物体，意见分歧则更大。

passages.en: The study found that shared taste was most common for faces and natural landscapes, but least common among works of architecture and art. The hypothesis is the commonly pleasing features, like proportion or symmetry, are at work.
passages.zh: 研究发现，共同审美趣味最常见于面孔和自然景观，而在建筑和艺术作品中最少见。其假设是，比例或对称性等通常能带来愉悦感的特征在其中发挥着作用。

passages.en: Preferences for natural scenes might be learned through life experiences. Factors like habitability, safety, and openness might be preferred as people develop. Some of the details of landscapes change, but the basics are more common, e.g., water, open spaces, and signs of care.
passages.zh: 人们对自然景观的偏好可能是在生活经历中逐渐形成的。随着人们的成长，宜居性、安全性和开阔感等因素可能会成为人们偏好的对象。景观的某些细节会发生变化，但基本要素更加普遍，例如水域、开阔空间以及受到照料的迹象。

passages.en: Art and architecture, unlike natural spaces, do not have the same level of exposure. So, people do not have the same level of shared taste.
passages.zh: 与自然空间不同，艺术和建筑并没有同等程度的接触机会。因此，人们也不会具有同等程度的共同审美趣味。

passages.en: It's possible that the lower amount of agreement in the shared taste of artifacts has to do more with elements of style, rather than "behavioral consequences".
passages.zh: 人们在人工制品方面共同审美趣味的一致性较低，可能更多与风格元素有关，而不是与“行为后果”有关。

passages.en: All of the consequences seem reasonable (or at least possible), but I think there might be an interesting philosophical conclusion that they did not draw. It seems that there is an objective ground to our aesthetic preferences or evaluations. I am not saying this would mean beauty is completely objective, just that there could possibly be general objective principles at work, i.e., beauty is not simply in the eye of the beholder.
passages.zh: 所有这些推论似乎都是合理的（或者至少是可能的），但我认为其中或许存在一个有趣的哲学结论，而他们没有得出这一结论。我们的审美偏好或评价似乎存在某种客观基础。我并不是说这意味着美完全是客观的，只是说，可能有一些普遍的客观原则在发挥作用；也就是说，美并不只是存在于观看者的眼中。

passages.en: Nature exhibits some of the universal aesthetic features, such as radiance, in a common way throughout the world. It's not exactly the same everywhere, but it is common. For example, a sunset is similar enough in different places to warrant almost universal appeal.
passages.zh: 自然以一种在世界各地都很常见的方式呈现出某些普遍的审美特征，例如光辉。它并非在任何地方都完全相同，但这种特征具有普遍性。比如，不同地方的日落足够相似，因此几乎能够引起普遍的喜爱。

passages.en: Possible universal principles of beauty—such as proportion, fittingness, radiance, and others—are general categories, which allow for a wide array of embodiments. When people get involved in making artifacts in architecture or art, they apply these very general concepts in unique ways. But the way they applied the principle may not have universal appeal.
passages.zh: 可能具有普遍性的美的原则，例如比例、合宜性、光辉以及其他原则，都是一般性的类别，因而可以有多种多样的具体体现。当人们参与建筑或艺术创作、制造人工制品时，他们会以独特的方式运用这些十分一般的概念。但他们运用这些原则的方式未必能获得普遍的认同。

passages.en: This is why it's important to experience diverse cultures and their artifacts because it opens us up to different ways of approaching or constructing beauty. And it is always good to question our assumptions.
passages.zh: 这就是为什么体验不同的文化及其人工制品很重要，因为这会让我们接触到构思或创造美的不同方式。而且，质疑我们的假设总是有益的。

questions.stem: What does the passage say about the statement "beauty is in the eye of the beholder"?
questions.stem_zh: 文章对"情人眼里出西施"这一说法是如何评价的?

options.text: It has hardly ever been disputed.
options.zh: 它几乎从未受到过质疑。

options.text: It can be interpreted aesthetically.
options.zh: 它可以从美学角度进行解读。

options.text: Many people have found it absurd.
options.zh: 许多人认为它很荒谬。

options.text: People have long been misled by it.
options.zh: 人们长期以来一直被它误导。

questions.判型: 题干 What does the passage say about the statement 把范围圈死在那句引语上，要求复述作者对它的具体描述，不是推断也不是主旨。
questions.拆句: What does the passage say about the statement "beauty is in the eye of the beholder"? 主干是 What does the passage say about X，X = the statement "beauty is in the eye of the beholder"；structure 平铺直叙，无陷阱。
questions.定位: P1 Statements, like "beauty is in the eye of the beholder(观看者)", are rarely questioned. 诸如「美在观看者的眼中」这样的说法，几乎从不受到质疑。

locate.en: Statements, like "beauty is in the eye of the beholder(观看者)", are rarely questioned.
locate.zh: 诸如「美在观看者的眼中」这样的说法，几乎从不受到质疑。

option_analysis.note: 预判「几乎无人质疑」与 hardly ever been disputed 在频率与语义上完全等值，锁定 A。
It can be interpreted aesthetically 说「它可被审美地解读」，与原文 rarely questioned 完全无关；作者只说「无人质疑」，没说「可被审美解读」。
原文说「人们觉得 absurd to think otherwise」（反着想才荒谬），而 Many people have found it absurd 把「荒谬」直接扣给那句谚语本身，正话反说。
People have long been misled by it 说「人们长期被它误导」，原文只说作者「想 push back 一下」，并未给该谚语贴「误导」标签。

questions.stem: What does a recent study exploring aesthetic taste show?
questions.stem_zh: 最近一项探索审美品味的研究显示了什么?

options.text: Aesthetic tastes tend to differ from person to person.
options.zh: 审美品味往往因人而异。

options.text: Natural beauty is rarely surpassed by artificial beauty.
options.zh: 自然美很少被人工美所超越。

options.text: There is less consensus on objects shaped by human craft.
options.zh: 人们对人工制品的共识较少。

options.text: There is general agreement on what is pleasing to the eye.
options.zh: 人们对什么是赏心悦目的存在普遍共识。

questions.判型: What does a recent study exploring aesthetic taste show 问的是一项具体研究 show 出什么——属于事实复述。
questions.拆句: What does a recent study exploring aesthetic taste show? 主干是 What does a study show；exploring aesthetic taste 是 study 的现在分词后置定语，作用是限定哪项研究。结构清晰，无陷阱。
questions.定位: P2 The results from this study show that people agree very much in their aesthetic evaluation of natural objects, but they disagree more about artifacts, or human-made objects. 这项研究的结果显示，人们对自然物的审美评价高度一致，但对人造物（即人工制造的物品）则分歧更多。

locate.en: The results from this study show that people agree very much in their aesthetic evaluation of natural objects, but they disagree more about artifacts, or human-made objects.
locate.zh: 这项研究的结果显示，人们对自然物的审美评价高度一致，但对人造物（即人工制造的物品）则分歧更多。

option_analysis.note: Aesthetic tastes tend to differ from person to person 把原文「人造物上分歧」扩大成「审美口味本来就因人而异」，丢掉了原文「自然物上一致」这一半。
Natural beauty is rarely surpassed by artificial beauty 把研究讲成「自然美几乎不被人造美超越」，原文谈的是「评价一致性」，不是「美的优劣比较」。
预判要求选项聚焦「人造物上分歧更多」，less consensus on objects shaped by human craft 完整对应该语义，锁 C。

pairs.orig: they disagree more about artifacts, or human-made objects
pairs.opt: less consensus on objects shaped by human craft

option_analysis.note: There is general agreement on what is pleasing to the eye 只说「人们对什么好看普遍一致」，丢掉了原文「对人造物分歧更多」这关键一半，与研究的对比结论不符。

questions.stem: Why do people differ in their aesthetic appraisal of artifacts?
questions.stem_zh: 为什么人们对人工制品的审美评价存在差异?

options.text: They come out in a great variety of designs.
options.zh: 它们的设计种类繁多。

options.text: They lead to varying behavioral consequences.
options.zh: 它们导致不同的行为后果。

options.text: They take up much less natural space than landscapes.
options.zh: 它们占用的自然空间比风景少得多。

options.text: They come into people's view less often than natural spaces.
options.zh: 它们进入人们视野的频率低于自然空间。

questions.判型: Why do people differ in their aesthetic appraisal of artifacts 问的是一项已写明的具体原因，不是让你推断作者的言外之意。
questions.拆句: Why do people differ in their aesthetic appraisal of artifacts? 一般疑问句结构 Why do S V O，differ in 是固定搭配（在某方面有差异）；无陷阱。
questions.定位: P5 Art and architecture, unlike natural spaces, do not have the same level of exposure. So, people do not have the same level of shared taste. 艺术与建筑（不像自然空间）没有同等程度的曝光度。因此，人们对它们的共同审美趣味也达不到同样的程度。

locate.en: Art and architecture, unlike natural spaces, do not have the same level of exposure. So, people do not have the same level of shared taste.
locate.zh: 艺术与建筑（不像自然空间）没有同等程度的曝光度。因此，人们对它们的共同审美趣味也达不到同样的程度。

option_analysis.note: They come out in a great variety of designs 谈的是「设计多样」，与原文给出的原因 exposure 完全无关；这是 P9 里 a wide array of embodiments 的话被移花接木过来。
P6 明说差异 has to do more with elements of style, rather than "behavioral consequences"——作者用 rather than 否定了 behavioral consequences；They lead to varying behavioral consequences 反而把被否定的那一支抬回来当原因。
They take up much less natural space than landscapes 说人造物比自然景观「占用的自然空间更少」，原文从未做过这种空间面积比较；这是按生活常识替原文补造的对比。
预判要求「人造物被看到的机会少」，与 come into people's view less often than natural spaces 完全等值，锁 D。

pairs.orig: do not have the same level of exposure
pairs.opt: come into people's view less often than natural spaces

questions.stem: What does the example of sunset tell about nature?
questions.stem_zh: 日落的例子说明了自然的什么特点?

options.text: It creates a powerful appeal through its brilliant radiance.
options.zh: 它通过灿烂的光辉产生强大的吸引力。

options.text: It displays aesthetic traits in a similar way the world over.
options.zh: 它在世界各地以相似的方式展现美学特征。

options.text: It embodies beauty with a wide array of aesthetic features.
options.zh: 它以广泛的美学特征体现美。

options.text: It establishes the principles of beauty in a number of ways.
options.zh: 它以多种方式确立了美的原则。

questions.判型: What does the example of sunset tell about nature 问的是举这个例子是为了告诉读者关于 nature 的什么——典型的「例证目的」考法。
questions.拆句: What does the example of sunset tell about nature? 主干 What does X tell about Y；tell 在此处意为 reveal / indicate（说明、揭示），不要按字面理解为「告诉某人某事」。
questions.定位: P8 Nature exhibits some of the universal aesthetic features, such as radiance, in a common way throughout the world. It's not exactly the same everywhere, but it is common. For example, a sunset is similar enough in different places to warrant almost universal appeal. 自然界以共通的方式在世界各地呈现某些普遍的审美特征（比如光辉）。各处并不完全相同，但确实有共通之处。例如，落日在不同地方足够相似，因而几乎能引起普世的吸引力。

locate.en: Nature exhibits some of the universal aesthetic features, such as radiance, in a common way throughout the world. It's not exactly the same everywhere, but it is common. For example, a sunset is similar enough in different places to warrant almost universal appeal.
locate.zh: 自然界以共通的方式在世界各地呈现某些普遍的审美特征（比如光辉）。各处并不完全相同，但确实有共通之处。例如，落日在不同地方足够相似，因而几乎能引起普世的吸引力。

option_analysis.note: It creates a powerful appeal through its brilliant radiance 谈的是「落日靠光辉本身创造强烈吸引力」，是 sunset 例子的表层描写，不是例子要说明的论点（共通性）。
预判要求「自然在全球以共通方式呈现审美特征」，It displays aesthetic traits in a similar way the world over 与论点句逐项匹配，锁 B。

pairs.orig: Nature exhibits some of the universal aesthetic features, such as radiance, in a common way throughout the world
pairs.opt: It displays aesthetic traits in a similar way the world over

option_analysis.note: It embodies beauty with a wide array of aesthetic features 借用 a wide array of embodiments 与 Possible universal principles of beauty 的短语，但 P9 谈的是「美的原则允许多样体现」，不是 sunset 例子要说明的内容。
It establishes the principles of beauty in a number of ways 把「sunset 例证一种共通呈现方式」夸大成「确立了多个美学原则」，原文从未把 sunset 提到「确立原则」的高度。

questions.stem: Why do artifacts not always hold universal appeal?
questions.stem_zh: 为什么人工制品并不总是具有普遍吸引力?

options.text: The appreciation of their beauty is not subject to objective standards.
options.zh: 对其美的欣赏不受客观标准的约束。

options.text: The universal principle of beauty prevents a wide array of embodiments.
options.zh: 美的普遍原则阻止了广泛的体现方式。

options.text: The way their creators apply the principle of beauty may not be pleasing to everybody.
options.zh: 其创作者应用美的原则的方式可能无法取悦所有人。

options.text: Their creators interpret the universal principle of beauty each in their preferred way.
options.zh: 其创作者各自以自己偏好的方式诠释美的普遍原则。

questions.判型: Why do artifacts not always hold universal appeal 仍是对已写明原因的复述问法，作者已经直接写出「为什么」，不是推断。
questions.拆句: Why do artifacts not always hold universal appeal? 否定副词 not always 表示「并非总是」（部分否定），不是「从来不」；不要错读成 never。
questions.定位: P9 When people get involved in making artifacts in architecture or art, they apply these very general concepts in unique ways. But the way they applied the principle may not have universal appeal. 当人们投身于建筑或艺术中的人造物创作时，他们以独特的方式运用这些非常宽泛的概念。但他们运用原则的方式未必能引起所有人的共鸣。

locate.en: When people get involved in making artifacts in architecture or art, they apply these very general concepts in unique ways. But the way they applied the principle may not have universal appeal.
locate.zh: 当人们投身于建筑或艺术中的人造物创作时，他们以独特的方式运用这些非常宽泛的概念。但他们运用原则的方式未必能引起所有人的共鸣。

option_analysis.note: The appreciation of their beauty is not subject to objective standards 说「人造物之美不受客观标准约束」，但作者在 P7 与 P9 都坚持存在 objective ground / Possible universal principles of beauty，A 与作者立场相反。
The universal principle of beauty prevents a wide array of embodiments 说原则「阻止」多样体现，原文恰恰说 are general categories, which allow for a wide array of embodiments——「允许」多样体现。
「运用方式」+「未必人人喜欢」两个语义落点在 The way their creators apply the principle of beauty may not be pleasing to everybody 都得到对应，锁 C。

pairs.orig: the way they applied the principle may not have universal appeal
pairs.opt: The way their creators apply the principle of beauty may not be pleasing to everybody

option_analysis.note: Their creators interpret the universal principle of beauty each in their preferred way 只说「创作者各自按偏好诠释原则」，并未传达「未必人人喜欢」这层「为何没有普遍吸引力」的因果；它只复述了 they apply these very general concepts in unique ways 的前半段，丢掉了 But 之后的关键否定。

translation.title: 2024年12月·第2套英语六级汉译英（段落翻译） · 客观介绍洋山港这一深水港 参考译文与解析
translation.directions: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to translate a passage from Chinese into English. You should write your answer on Answer Sheet 2.
translation.source_zh: 洋山港(Yangshan Port)是上海航运中心的重要组成部分,是中国第一个深水港,也是世界上规模最大的深水港之一。经过近20年的发展,洋山港已实现高度自动化。数字技术和人工智能的使用大大减少了用工成本和碳排放。自主研发的码头管理系统可以在百公里之外对大型设备进行远程操控。洋山港看上去一片繁忙,现场却见不到人工操作,而且能够24小时不间断运作。洋山港将不断发展,为把上海建成一个全球航运中心做出更大贡献。
translation.reference_en:
Yangshan Port is an important part of the Shanghai shipping center, China's first deep-water port, and one of the largest deep-water ports in the world. After nearly two decades of development, it has achieved a high level of automation. The use of digital technology and artificial intelligence has greatly reduced labor costs and carbon emissions. The self-developed terminal management system can remotely control large equipment from hundreds of kilometers away. The port looks busy, but no manual operation can be seen on site, and it can operate around the clock without interruption. Yangshan Port will continue to develop and make greater contributions to building Shanghai into a global shipping center.
【衔接】
第1→2句:用代词承接避免重复主语第1句主语已是 Yangshan Port,第2句若再重复 Yangshan Port 显啰嗦,改用代词 it 承接(After nearly two decades of development, it has achieved...),让指代清楚又不重复。
第2→3句:由"已自动化"引出"靠什么实现"第2句说港口已实现高度自动化,第3句正是解释自动化的手段(数字技术和人工智能),信息上是承接关系,顺序保持"先结果后手段"即可,无需强加连接词,但可让两句话题(自动化—技术应用)自然衔接。
第5句内部:转折与递进连词显化看上去一片繁忙,现场却见不到人工操作 的"却"必须用 but/yet 显化,而且 用 and 显化,否则三分句堆在一起读着松散,英文须靠连词把转折、递进这两层逻辑摆出来。
第6句:用 Yangshan Port 回扣首句收尾结尾句重新点出 Yangshan Port(而非一直用 it),与首句的 Yangshan Port 首尾呼应,使整篇结构完整、收束有力,读者清楚展望的主体仍是洋山港。

cohesion.detail: 第2句说港口已实现高度自动化,第3句正是解释自动化的手段(数字技术和人工智能),信息上是承接关系,顺序保持"先结果后手段"即可,无需强加连接词,但可让两句话题(自动化—技术应用)自然衔接。
